body:
Determination: the GLOBAL observation-cursor behaviour (Record A) applies to this workspace's integration. The observation cursor is a single, global, filter-independent, monotonic durable position. Record B's "per-consumer" claim is not a store/contract property: it at most describes the fact that a consumer retains the opaque cursor value it was handed (so two consumers may sit at different positions); the contract's position space itself is one shared sequence, and as a contract statement for the current pinned line B is incorrect.

Why, in order:

1) The conflict is real and cannot be ranked by its own metadata. docs/engineering/09-observation-contract-a.md ("global — one position shared by all readers of the store") and -b.md ("per-consumer — each consumer holds its own independent position") both declare "Status: normative" and "Version scope: current pinned line". Same version scope, same status, mutually exclusive statements about the same proposition, no dates/revisions/supersession markers -> neither temporal scope nor explicit supersession separates them.

2) Neither copy has provenance standing locally. docs/engineering/README.md's archive index registers `09-adaptive-allocation-spec.md` (PLMP-ALC) as #09 and omits both observation files; its closing rule puts spec status on the SDS last-revision record and makes registered archive specs prevail. More decisively, the observation-cursor contract is Ordarium's: "Ordarium 合同以其仓库 docs/12–17 为准" and "本仓库不复制其文本，只引用" (00-heritage.md §5; 07-ordarium-alignment.md 权威序 §1.2/§3). Unindexed, unauthored local prose copies of a contract this repo does not own cannot outrank the pinned integration artifact.

3) The pinned integration artifact is local and states the semantics explicitly. package.json / pnpm-workspace.yaml pin ordarium-v1.3.1 (installed @ordarium/core@1.3.1). @ordarium/core types.d.ts defines the state-change feed (ORD-BOOT-0) page as `cursor: string` = "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change", with `namespace` on the filter only narrowing observation ("absent observes every namespace"), exposed via the `stateChangeFeed` capability. @ordarium/ledger-sqlite's `changes()` implements and comments it: "Semantic validation against the global high-water mark (ORD-BOOT-0.1): the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence. Concurrent commits only raise the mark... a restored/replaced ledger lowers it and fails closed" (InvalidCursorError). There is no per-consumer cursor registry anywhere in the kernel.

4) Palimpsest's own observation face has the same shape, so the conclusion does not depend on reading the ledger comment as the contract. GET /api/graph computes `changed: cursorParam === null || Number(cursorParam) !== graph.project.cursor` (src/serve.ts) against one canonical event position with no per-reader server state; `serviceHealth()` returns that same global `eventCursor` (src/tools/controller.ts). The only non-global token is `viewCursor` = `v1:<epoch>:<eventCursor>:<viewGeneration>`, which spec 35 defines as per-process-epoch and explicitly separates (VIEW-INV-1 EventCursor ≠ ViewCursor); it is not a per-consumer cursor.

Conclusion: global governs — one shared, filter-independent durable position, monotonically non-decreasing under concurrent commits, failing closed when a cursor cannot be justified by the ledger's own history. Residual hygiene (not a blocker for this determination): the two unindexed local copies should be removed or corrected since this repo does not own that contract text; if Record B was intended for a different surface (e.g., a future per-consumer feed), it needs its own owner/revision anchor.

Cannot legitimately finalize which observation-cursor behaviour applies: two load-bearing normative sources in this workspace contradict each other, and the authority that could rank them belongs to the peer that owns the contract, which has not responded.

Why the conflict is real and not locally rankable:
- docs/engineering/09-observation-contract-a.md: "the observation cursor semantics contract is GLOBAL — one position shared by all readers of the store"; docs/engineering/09-observation-contract-b.md: "PER-CONSUMER — each consumer holds its own independent position". Both carry identical metadata: "Status: normative", "Version scope: current pinned line". No date, revision, or supersession marker; so neither version scope, temporal scope, nor explicit supersession separates them.
- Neither has provenance standing locally: docs/engineering/README.md's archive index registers `09-adaptive-allocation-spec.md` (PLMP-ALC) as #09 and omits both observation files; its closing rule defers spec status to the SDS last-revision record and makes registered archive specs prevail. More decisively, the contract is Ordarium-owned: 00-heritage.md §5 ("Ordarium 侧合同…以 Ordarium 仓库 docs/12–17 与 evidence/ 为准；本仓库不复制其文本，只引用") and 07-ordarium-alignment.md (权威序 §1.2/§3). Both local files are unauthored copies of a contract this repo explicitly does not own, so neither can outrank the other.
- Local corroborating evidence leans one way but is not the authority: the pinned integration line is ordarium-v1.3.1 (package.json + pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides; installed @ordarium/core@1.3.1). @ordarium/core types.d.ts defines the observation page cursor as an "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change" (namespace only narrows; ORD-BOOT-0), and @ordarium/ledger-sqlite `changes()` validates the caller cursor against the ledger-wide global high-water mark and fails closed when a restored/replaced ledger lowers it. Palimpsest's own /api/graph cursor is likewise one canonical global event position (viewCursor is a separate per-process token, spec 35 VIEW-INV-1). This supports the "global" reading (Record A) with per-consumer retention being only caller-side bookkeeping, but a shipped dependency's compiled comments are not the frozen contract text for the current pinned line, and no accepted owner authority confirms it.

Escalation already performed (no response yet):
- Posted a boundary question to ordarium.main (owner) as evt_b116d17f-d0aa-4f0a-8a1d-c38dbdbcc338 in thread thr_4c3bc8eb-3d0f-426e-96ee-fe5fc52f6c56, asking for the authoritative semantics plus a spec anchor (e.g. ORD-BOOT-0 §).
- Proposed BoundaryContract `obs-cursor-semantics` revision 1 (termsDigest 6afec2aeaec1d86d22f173ab8f4edd3436aea1d2f1390d688c4e2304af1ce550) whose acceptance criterion is exactly that owner statement. It remains status=draft with acceptedBy=[], and repeated collab_inbox polls return no batch.

Disposition: unresolved. The decision requires the owner's authoritative statement for the current pinned line; once ordarium.main confirms (or accepts the contract), the determination can be finalized — the evidence on file currently points to the global/filter-independent position semantics (Record A), with Record B's per-consumer claim describing only caller-side cursor retention, not the contract's position space.
